subject: Archaeology
title: The Antikythera Shipwreck
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Antikythera Shipwreck.

hook.text: Greek sponge divers found a Roman shipwreck in 1900 that contained the world's first known analog computer.

buildup.text: The ship sank around 60 BCE near Antikythera island, carrying bronze statues, jewelry, glassware, and coins.

discovery.text: Among the corroded lumps was a gear mechanism with over 30 bronze wheels — it predicted eclipses and planetary.

twist.text: Nothing this complex appeared again for 1,400 years. The technology was lost when Rome fell and was not reinvented.

climax.text: X-ray imaging in 2006 revealed inscriptions and gear teeth. The full device is now digitally reconstructed.

punchline.text: Ancient Greeks built a computer. The sea hid it for 2,000 years.

quiz.question: What was the Antikythera Mechanism used for?
options: Navigating ships across the open Mediterranean
Predicting eclipses and tracking planetary positions
Calculating taxes owed to the Roman Senate
